title: USDA Publishes Annual Dairy Import-Licensing Notices for the 2027 Quota Year
summary: USDA's Foreign Agricultural Service published two routine Federal Register notices on Sept. 2 governing the Dairy Tariff-Rate Quota (TRQ) import licensing program: one sets the 2027 license fee at $325 per license (total program cost estimated at $631,516 across roughly 1,950 licenses), and the other shifts specified quota amounts for certain dairy articles from the historical license category to the lottery (nonhistorical) category for the 2027 quota year.
why_it_matters: These are routine annual administrative filings, not a policy change, but they set the mechanics — fees and license-category allocations — for who can import quota-limited dairy ingredients in 2027. Worth a line in the trade-policy file given the active, high-profile US-Canada dairy tariff dispute already on the company's radar.
recommended_action: No action needed; file for reference alongside the broader US-Canada tariff tracking.
date_evidence: url slug

title: Survey Finds Rising Recall Volume Is Eroding Consumer Trust and Buying Behavior
summary: A consumer survey commissioned by GS1 US found FDA posted 26 food recall notices in August 2026 alone, and that 67% of consumers now say they've avoided an entire food category after just one recall notice, up from 60% a year earlier; 94% say they are concerned about how often food is recalled, and the share who believe the recall system effectively protects public health fell to 80% from 85%. GS1 US published the findings via a Sept. 2 press release, with same-day coverage from Fortune and Food Safety Magazine.
why_it_matters: Dairy products have accounted for a significant share of 2026's recall notices (cottage cheese, soft cheese tied to a multiyear Listeria outbreak, ice cream), so this data quantifies a real category-avoidance risk tied to recall volume and reinforces the case for clear, fast recall communications and proactive trust-building messaging.
recommended_action: Share the survey findings with communications and consumer-insights teams; use as supporting data when reviewing the recall-response and consumer-trust messaging playbook.
date_evidence: url slug (fortune.com/2026/09/02/...); PRNewswire release dated Sept. 2, 2026

title: California Legislature Passes First-of-Its-Kind 'Non-Ultraprocessed Certified' Food Label Bill
summary: California's Assembly Bill 2244 cleared the Legislature on Aug. 31 with unanimous votes (32-0 in the Senate, 72-0 in the Assembly) and was sent to Gov. Gavin Newsom on Sept. 1. The bill creates a voluntary state certification seal, "Non-Ultraprocessed Certified," for products meeting standards that exclude synthetic dyes, flavor enhancers, non-sugar sweeteners and certain processing aids; Newsom has until Sept. 30, 2026 to sign or veto it and is reportedly expected to sign.
why_it_matters: This would be the first state-level certification program built around a UPF definition, giving California a template other states may copy; because the qualifying criteria touch additives, flavor enhancers, non-sugar sweeteners and processing aids common in flavored milk, cultured dairy and processed cheese, it creates both a potential marketing opportunity for compliant products and a competitive/labeling distinction for products that would not qualify.
recommended_action: Brief labeling/regulatory affairs on AB 2244 ahead of the Sept. 30 gubernatorial deadline; assess which products in the portfolio could qualify for the voluntary seal and which would be excluded under its additive criteria.
date_evidence: url slug (bakeryandsnacks.com/Article/2026/09/01/...)

title: CDC/FDA Close Second Infant-Formula Botulism Outbreak, Trace It to Same Dairy Supplier as Prior Outbreak
summary: CDC and FDA formally closed the investigation into a multistate infant botulism outbreak linked to Nara Organics powdered infant formula (four infants hospitalized in California, Pennsylvania and Washington, onset April-May 2026, no deaths) after whole-genome sequencing and supply-chain records traced the contamination to the same two suppliers implicated in the 2025 ByHeart infant formula botulism outbreak, which hospitalized 48 infants in 19 states: Organic West Milk (raw organic milk) and Dairy Farmers of America (spray-drying). FDA also noted that Organic West Milk had earlier given the agency an incomplete customer list during the ByHeart investigation that omitted Nara Organics.
why_it_matters: This is the second national infant-health outbreak traced to the same organic whole-milk supply chain within about a year, and FDA's finding that a supplier withheld a customer name during an active federal investigation raises the likelihood of tighter agency scrutiny of organic dairy ingredient sourcing, spray-drying practices and supplier traceability industry-wide. No product or facility of the company is implicated, but any manufacturer sourcing organic milk powder, or working with the same cooperative network, should expect closer buyer due-diligence and possible new FDA traceability expectations for dairy ingredient suppliers.
recommended_action: Brief supply-chain/quality leadership on the Organic West Milk-Dairy Farmers of America link; confirm no shared sourcing exposure and monitor for any FDA follow-up guidance on organic dairy ingredient traceability.
date_evidence: CDC outbreak investigation page marks closure Aug. 27, 2026, corroborated by Food Safety News reporting

title: Chobani to Invest $1.2B in Pennsylvania Plant, Buying Back Keurig Dr Pepper's Equity Stake
summary: Chobani will invest approximately $1.2 billion to acquire and expand a former Keurig Dr Pepper manufacturing plant in Allentown, Pennsylvania, adding more than 900 jobs and building a 1.5-million-square-foot campus expected to source over 3 billion pounds of Pennsylvania milk annually at full capacity. As part of the transaction, Chobani is buying back Keurig Dr Pepper's roughly $800 million equity stake in the company and separately paying $125 million for the plant itself, as KDP works to reduce debt; the Allentown project is part of a more than $4 billion buildout of Chobani's U.S. manufacturing network.
why_it_matters: A major new capacity buildout by a leading yogurt/dairy processor signals rising competition for Northeast milk supply and expanding scale in the category; it carries no direct regulatory or reputational exposure for the company but is worth tracking for regional milk-sourcing and pricing dynamics and shifting competitive positioning.
recommended_action: Track regional milk-sourcing and capacity dynamics in the Northeast; no direct action needed now.
date_evidence: url slug (Bloomberg: /2026-09-01/; PR Newswire release dated Sept. 1, 2026)

title: House Subcommittee Advances Bipartisan Bills to Federalize Packaging 'Recyclable' and 'Recycled Content' Claims
summary: On Sept. 1, 2026, the House Energy and Commerce Committee's Commerce, Manufacturing and Trade Subcommittee voice-voted to advance the PACK Act (H.R. 6832) and the Recycled Materials Attribution Act (H.R. 7502) to the full committee. The bills would set federal, third-party-certified standards for "recyclable," "compostable," "reusable" and "recycled content" packaging claims and would preempt the current patchwork of state rules; RMAA would also formally recognize mass-balance accounting for recycled-content claims.
why_it_matters: A single federal packaging-claims standard would ease compliance for a national dairy manufacturer navigating inconsistent state EPR and labeling laws (CA, CO, ME, MD, MN, OR, WA), but the mass-balance provision is already drawing greenwashing criticism from environmental advocates -- any packaging using recycled-content claims should be ready for scrutiny if the bills advance further.
recommended_action: Monitor Only; revisit if the bills clear full committee markup or draw greenwashing criticism naming specific brands or packaging claims.

title: Chobani to Invest $1.2 Billion in New Pennsylvania Milk-Processing Hub
summary: Chobani announced Sept. 1 it will invest approximately $1.2 billion over five years to convert a former Keurig Dr Pepper facility in Allentown, Pennsylvania into a 1.5-million-square-foot milk production and warehouse campus, creating more than 900 jobs. Gov. Josh Shapiro's office called it the largest private-sector investment in Pennsylvania agriculture history; at full capacity the plant is expected to source more than 3 billion pounds of Pennsylvania milk annually, roughly 30% of the state's current milk production.
why_it_matters: A major competitor's large-scale capacity build signals continued consolidation and investment in US dairy processing and will compete for regional raw-milk supply; the scale (the largest-ever Pennsylvania agriculture investment) is likely to draw sustained trade and local media coverage that could prompt comparison questions.
recommended_action: Monitor regional coverage and Pennsylvania milk-supply competition effects; no action needed unless asked to comment on the announcement.
date_evidence: Pennsylvania Governor's Office press release dated Sept. 1, 2026, corroborated by same-day trade press

title: USDA Sets 2027 Dairy Import License Fee at $325, Updates Safeguard Trigger Levels
summary: USDA's Foreign Agricultural Service published a Federal Register notice Sept. 2 setting the 2027 tariff-rate-quota-year dairy import license fee at $325 per license, down from $350 in 2026, based on an estimated $631,516 total administrative cost spread across roughly 1,950 expected licenses. A companion notice updated the quantity-based safeguard trigger levels and license-transfer amounts that apply to dairy products under the 2027 TRQ year.
why_it_matters: Routine annual administrative notice for companies that hold USDA dairy import licenses under the tariff-rate-quota system; no policy change, but the updated safeguard trigger levels are a detail import-dependent processors should log for 2027 planning.
recommended_action: No action needed; forward to trade/import compliance team as a 2027 planning reference.
date_evidence: Federal Register publication date Sept. 2, 2026 (document 2026-17954)

title: EPA and Army Corps Reopen Public Comment on WOTUS Water Definition Ahead of Final Rule
summary: On Sept. 4, 2026, EPA and the US Army Corps of Engineers issued a Supplemental Notice of Proposed Rulemaking seeking additional public input on how to define "waters of the United States" (WOTUS) under the Clean Water Act, including the definitions of "relatively permanent" waters and a "continuous surface water connection." The agencies say they are advancing toward a "durable final rule" after receiving more than 22,000 comments on their original November 2025 proposal; the new comment window opens for 30 days once the supplemental notice is published in the Federal Register, expected within about a week.
why_it_matters: WOTUS jurisdiction determines which farm ditches, wetlands and on-site waters require Clean Water Act permits before discharge or fill activity, directly affecting dairy farms and processing facilities that manage wastewater or stormwater; a narrower "relatively permanent" standard would ease permitting burden across the dairy supply chain, while a broader one would expand it, so this fresh comment window is a chance to weigh in before the definition is finalized.
recommended_action: Monitor for the Federal Register publication and confirmed comment deadline; no action needed until the proposal's substantive definitions are released.
date_evidence: EPA news release dated Sept. 4, 2026, corroborated by same-day Agri-Pulse, Morning Ag Clips and KFGO coverage

title: ByHeart and IDFA Funded the FDA-Adjacent Report Reviewing Their Own Infant-Formula Botulism Outbreaks
summary: The Reagan-Udall Foundation for the FDA published "Applying the Science of Infant Formula Safety," a 44-page report stemming from a July 13, 2026 roundtable on Clostridium botulinum in powdered infant formula that was convened in collaboration with, and paid for by, ByHeart and the International Dairy Foods Association (IDFA) — the company and dairy trade association tied to the 2025-2026 botulism outbreaks that hospitalized roughly 50 infants. The report issues 22 non-binding recommendations on testing and prevention; none of its 24 listed contributors is a parent of an affected infant.
why_it_matters: IDFA speaks for the US dairy manufacturing industry broadly, so press criticism that the trade association and an implicated company funded a review of their own outbreak — with no mandatory rule proposed and no affected families involved — is a reputational exposure that can extend to dairy processors generally, particularly around industry self-funded science and testing-standard credibility (the report found the legacy SRC test can miss contamination that PCR testing catches). Any manufacturer relying on IDFA's advocacy or sharing organic milk-powder suppliers with the earlier outbreaks should expect continued questions about industry-funded safety reviews.
recommended_action: Brief communications/government-affairs leadership on the funding-transparency criticism before reporters ask whether the company backs IDFA's role; confirm no shared exposure via the Organic West Milk/Dairy Farmers of America supply chain already tracked from the Nara Organics item.
date_evidence: Reagan-Udall Foundation publication page indexed with a Sept. 3, 2026 publish date; syndicated criticism coverage (Marler Blog, EDairy News) followed within the next few days — established via search results in web-search fetch mode, not a directly viewed byline, since direct site access is blocked in this environment

title: USDA Unveils Plan to Modernize Agricultural Data Collection
summary: USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins announced a "Data Modernization Plan" at the Farm Progress Show on Sept. 1, aiming to reduce producer reporting burden, expand use of administrative data and mobile survey access, and modernize data infrastructure and geospatial tools (including higher-resolution Cropland Data Layer imagery). The plan follows a February 2026 request for public input and a series of state-fair and farm-show listening sessions held through August.
why_it_matters: USDA collects extensive mandatory and voluntary data from dairy processors (NASS surveys, dairy price/production reporting, and the pending Farm Bill's proposed mandatory dairy-processing cost-reporting framework tied to FMMO pricing, already on the watch list); how USDA implements this plan could change reporting formats, frequency, or burden for manufacturers, though no specific new dairy requirement was announced.
recommended_action: Monitor for specifics on how the plan applies to existing USDA dairy reporting programs; no action needed now.

title: IDFA-Backed SNAP Milk Incentive Program "Add Milk!" Expands to Oklahoma
summary: The Healthy Fluid Milk Incentive project "Add Milk!", championed by IDFA and funded via a $2.99M USDA grant to Auburn University's Hunger Solutions Institute, launched at three Tulsa-area stores in late August, giving SNAP participants a dollar-for-dollar match on qualifying low-fat, non-fat and lactose-free milk purchases. The expansion brings the program to more than 1,200 stores across 32 states.
why_it_matters: A positive, verifiable industry-backed nutrition-access story that gives dairy manufacturers a concrete talking point on milk affordability and SNAP access, complementing IDFA's other recently tracked school-nutrition commitments.
recommended_action: Usable as a proof point in nutrition-access/affordability messaging; no direct action needed.

title: NMPF's Longtime Trade-Policy Chief Jaime Castaneda to Retire in December
summary: National Milk Producers Federation announced Sept. 4 that Executive Vice President Jaime Castaneda, who has led NMPF and the U.S. Dairy Export Council's international trade-policy work since joining in 1999, will retire from NMPF in December 2026 after 27 years. He plans to continue serving as Executive Director of the Consortium for Common Food Names and remain engaged with USDEC and other food and agricultural organizations.
why_it_matters: Castaneda has been a lead architect of US dairy's export and trade-policy positioning, including USMCA dairy-access disputes and geographic-indication fights, and his exit lands during an active period of US-Canada tariff negotiations and unresolved USMCA dairy-compliance grievances. NMPF has not announced a successor, making the transition worth tracking but not yet a cause for concern.
recommended_action: Monitor for a successor announcement; no action needed.
date_evidence: Red River Farm Network byline/URL dated Sept. 4, 2026; matches NMPF press-release date

title: Canada's Retaliatory Tariffs on US Dairy Take Effect, Hitting Milk at 50% and Cheese at 25%
summary: Canada's "dollar-for-dollar" retaliatory tariffs on roughly $20-28 billion of US goods took effect at 12:01 a.m. Sept. 8, 2026, after weeks of confirmed lead time. Milk, cream and dairy ingredients (whey, caseinates, lactose) are taxed at 50%; finished cheese at 25% — matching the rates the US had imposed on Canadian dairy, alcohol and auto imports under Section 338/232 tariffs after talks collapsed Aug. 22.
why_it_matters: This is the actual go-live of tariffs this system has tracked since Aug. 22, not a new announcement — US dairy and dairy-ingredient exporters to Canada now face materially higher landed costs with no resumed-talks date announced, and ingredient exporters (whey, caseinates, lactose) face a steeper 50% rate than finished cheese at 25%.
recommended_action: Confirm current Canada-bound export exposure at the now-effective 50%/25% rates; watch for any sign of resumed US-Canada talks before assuming this is the settled state.
date_evidence: url slug (cnbc.com/2026/09/08/) and CBS News same-day report

title: Long Island Deli Producer Recalls All Cream Cheese and Deli Salads for Listeria — Third Recall at the Plant in a Year
summary: Made Fresh Salads, Inc. of Bay Shore, NY recalled every ready-to-eat deli-style salad and cream cheese product it makes on Sept. 6, 2026, after FDA and company environmental sampling found Listeria monocytogenes in the production facility. Affected products, sold to New York City-area retailers and distributors under the Made Fresh Salads and Northside labels with expiration dates through Sept. 18, have caused no reported illnesses. It is the plant's third Listeria-related recall in under a year, following a fall-2025 salad recall and a February-2026 cream cheese and tofu spread recall.
why_it_matters: Cream cheese is a dairy-category product, and a repeat-offender facility drawing renewed FDA scrutiny keeps Listeria in the food-safety news cycle even though this recall is confined to one small regional producer with no national branded dairy manufacturer involved; it's a reminder of the reputational spillover risk recalls carry for the wider dairy case.
recommended_action: Monitor for any expansion of the recall or linked illnesses; no direct action needed given the isolated regional scope.
date_evidence: FDA recall notice date, corroborated by trade coverage

title: Dairy Foods Names Wells Enterprises' Dunkirk, NY Ice Cream Plant Its 2026 Plant of the Year
summary: Dairy Foods magazine named Wells Enterprises' Dunkirk, New York ice cream and novelties facility (maker of Blue Bunny, Nutella Ice Cream and Kinder Bueno Frozen products) its 2026 Plant of the Year, citing a multi-year, multi-million-dollar expansion begun in 2024 that state officials estimate will generate roughly $891 million in local economic benefit over ten years.
why_it_matters: A positive trade-press showcase of dairy-sector manufacturing investment and capacity growth; useful as an industry benchmark and potential talking point on domestic manufacturing investment, with no direct exposure for the company.
recommended_action: No action needed; useful as a positive industry benchmark if manufacturing-investment talking points are needed.

title: Industry-Funded Report on Infant Formula Botulism Outbreaks Draws Criticism Over Lack of Mandatory Rules
summary: The Reagan-Udall Foundation for the FDA published "Applying the Science of Infant Formula Safety," a report from a July 13 roundtable on Clostridium botulinum risk in powdered infant formula that was funded and co-prepared by ByHeart Inc. and the International Dairy Foods Association (IDFA). The report offers 22 recommendations on testing, data-sharing and supply-chain controls but sets no mandatory requirements; critics note no parent or patient advocate participated in the roundtable.
why_it_matters: IDFA, the dairy industry's primary trade association, funded and helped prepare the report, and the ingredient at the center of the underlying outbreaks (organic powdered whole milk supplied by Organic West Milk and processed by Dairy Farmers of America) sits squarely in the dairy supply chain. Renewed coverage framing this as industry policing itself carries reputational exposure for dairy trade groups and ingredient suppliers even where a given manufacturer is not implicated.
recommended_action: Brief leadership on IDFA's role and prepare a short holding statement in case of press inquiries about industry-funded safety reviews; no proactive outreach needed.

title: Trump Administration Bans Imports of Canadian Dairy, Alcohol and Motorcycles in Trade War Escalation
summary: President Trump signed a series of proclamations under Section 338 banning imports of certain Canadian dairy products (including whey), most alcoholic beverages, motorcycles and molasses, effective Sept. 29, 2026. The action followed Canada's dollar-for-dollar retaliatory tariffs taking effect Sept. 8 and cites Canada's continued failure to remove what the administration calls discrimination against US dairy commerce after trade talks collapsed in August.
why_it_matters: This is a step beyond tariffs to an outright import ban, directly restricting the Canadian-origin whey and other dairy ingredients some US processors source, adding fresh supply-chain and sourcing uncertainty on top of the existing 50%/25% tariff regime already in effect. NMPF and IDFA both voiced support for pressure on Canada over USMCA dairy-access commitments while cautioning that a prolonged trade war raises costs and uncertainty for US processors, with no resumed-talks date announced.
recommended_action: Brief leadership on the Sept. 29 effective date and confirm any current reliance on Canadian-sourced whey or other affected dairy ingredients before then; watch for a Canadian counter-response.
date_evidence: url slug (washingtonpost.com/2026/09/08/) and same-day NBC News report

title: EPA and Army Publish Supplemental WOTUS Proposal, Opening 30-Day Comment Period
summary: EPA and the Army Corps of Engineers published a Supplemental Notice of Proposed Rulemaking in the Federal Register on Sept. 9, 2026 (Document 2026-18317), seeking further public input on how to define "waters of the United States" under the Clean Water Act, including the "relatively permanent" waters and "continuous surface water connection" tests. The agencies previously received roughly 220,000 comments on their November 2025 proposal and are using this supplement to narrow toward a final rule implementing the Supreme Court's Sackett v. EPA decision. Comments are due by Oct. 9, 2026.
why_it_matters: WOTUS jurisdiction determines which on-farm and processing-facility waters and wetlands require Clean Water Act permits, so dairy farms and plants with on-site water features have a fresh, now firmly dated window to weigh in before the agencies finalize the rule.
recommended_action: Monitor; note the Oct. 9 comment deadline for any environmental/regulatory affairs team considering a submission.
date_evidence: Federal Register publication date (Document 2026-18317)

title: 76 Dairy Companies and Co-ops Join NMPF, IDFA in Urging Congress to Reject Ultra-Processed Warning-Label Bill
summary: The National Milk Producers Federation and International Dairy Foods Association, joined by 76 dairy companies, cooperatives and state and regional producer organizations, sent congressional leaders a letter urging rejection of S. 5026, the Childhood Diabetes Reduction Act of 2026. The bill would create a broad "ultra-processed foods" definition and require front-of-package warning labels on foods it covers, including whole milk, cheese and most yogurts. NMPF President and CEO Gregg Doud said the bill "gets the science wrong, lumping wholesome dairy foods in with products that have nothing in common with them nutritionally."
why_it_matters: S. 5026 already awaits a Senate floor vote (tracked on the watch list) and would apply blanket UPF warning labels to nutrient-dense dairy staples; this coalition letter shows the scale of industry mobilization against it just ahead of that vote, raising the visibility of the messaging fight and giving the company a clear industry position to weigh alignment with.
recommended_action: Brief leadership on the coalition letter and confirm the company's own positioning relative to NMPF/IDFA messaging before any Senate floor vote on S. 5026.
date_evidence: secondary trade-press coverage (Cowsmo, EDairy News) consistently dated Sept. 9, 2026; NMPF's own release page could not be directly fetched in this web-search fetch-mode run

title: IDFA Names New Executive Council, Outlines Enhanced Governance Structure
summary: The International Dairy Foods Association announced new members of its Executive Council and outlined changes to its governance structure, refreshing the leadership body that oversees the trade association's business and operations. IDFA is governed by the Executive Council alongside five Industry Segment Boards (fluid milk, ice cream, cheese, yogurt/cultured products, dairy-derived ingredients) that set strategic and policy direction.
why_it_matters: IDFA is the primary trade association representing US dairy processors and manufacturers on issues now in active play — the pending New York GRAS-disclosure bill, the US-Canada dairy trade dispute, and opposition to S. 5026's ultra-processed-food warning-label mandate; new Executive Council leadership shapes how those advocacy priorities are carried forward.
recommended_action: No action needed; noted for awareness of IDFA leadership continuity.
date_evidence: IDFA news release page (search-indexed publication date Sept 9, 2026)

title: Whole Foods Recalls Specialty Cheese for Undeclared Egg Allergen
summary: Whole Foods Market issued an FDA-posted allergy alert for Fromagerie Coop de Mean's Cabricharme cheese, sold by the piece in the Specialty cheese department at 18 stores across seven states (Arizona, California, Connecticut, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York and Rhode Island), after discovering the product contains undeclared egg lysozyme. All best-by dates through Oct. 7, 2026 are affected; the mislabeling was caught by a store team member and no illnesses have been reported.
why_it_matters: A narrow, single-retailer allergen-labeling lapse on an imported specialty cheese with no illnesses and no dairy-processor involvement; included for tracking as a routine reminder that allergen-declaration diligence on specialty/soft cheese remains an active recall category.
recommended_action: No action needed; monitor for any expansion or illness reports.
date_evidence: FDA recall notice publication date

title: Dairy Farmers of America Withdraws From IDFA Over Milk-Pricing Reform Petition
summary: Dairy Farmers of America (DFA), the nation's largest dairy cooperative with 83 processing facilities, announced it is ending its membership in the International Dairy Foods Association (IDFA) after IDFA proceeded with a USDA petition to change how "make allowances" (estimated processing costs) are set in the Federal Milk Marketing Order system without full membership consensus. DFA said the move put it in the untenable position of appearing to endorse a milk-pricing policy position it believes conflicts with its farmer-owners' interests; IDFA had pursued the single-issue petition ahead of the National Milk Producers Federation, which is separately asking USDA to consider more comprehensive FMMO pricing changes.
why_it_matters: This is a rare, public fracture between the dairy industry's two largest trade associations over federal milk-pricing reform, a process that directly affects processor input costs; it signals the FMMO make-allowance fight is deepening rather than resolving, and comes as IDFA and NMPF have otherwise presented a unified front on other issues like this year's ultra-processed-food warning-label fight (S. 5026).
recommended_action: Monitor for additional co-op withdrawals, IDFA/NMPF statements, and how USDA responds to the competing FMMO make-allowance petitions; no action needed now.
date_evidence: reported Sept. 14, 2026 by Agri-Pulse, corroborated same-day by Dairy Herd and FoodBev Media

title: Consumer and Environmental Groups Rally Against FRESH Act Food-Safety Preemption Bill
summary: The Environmental Working Group held a Capitol Hill rally today opposing the FRESH Act (H.R. 8578), introduced in the House in April 2026, which would make FDA the sole regulator of food chemicals and additives and preempt state food-safety laws such as PFAS-in-packaging bans, artificial-dye restrictions in school food, and infant-formula heavy-metal disclosure requirements. Several members of Congress joined the rally opposing the bill, which remains in the House Agriculture Committee with no scheduled markup since referral.
why_it_matters: The FRESH Act's preemption clause would directly override several state food-safety laws already on this watch list, including New York's pending GRAS-disclosure and infant-formula heavy-metal-testing bills, so its trajectory affects how much state-level regulatory patchwork risk persists; today's rally signals the opposition coalition (EWG, consumer and public-health groups, several House Democrats) is escalating public pressure while the bill itself remains stalled in committee with no near-term legislative action expected.
recommended_action: No action needed now; continue tracking whether the FRESH Act gains committee movement given its interaction with pending state GRAS/labeling bills already on the watch list.
date_evidence: EWG press release describing the rally as held Tuesday, Sept. 15, 2026

title: Danone Recalls So Delicious Dairy-Free Frozen Dessert Over Foreign Material
summary: Danone US issued a voluntary nationwide recall on Sept. 15, 2026 of So Delicious Dairy Free Salted Caramel Cluster Non-Dairy Frozen Dessert pints (best-by dates on or before April 3, 2028) after consumer complaints found small stones and other hard foreign objects within the cashew inclusions. No injuries have been reported; the FDA has been notified and the recalled product was distributed to retail stores nationwide.
why_it_matters: This is the second Danone-brand US recall in under two months, following a July 2026 recall of YoCrunch products for embedded plastic pieces, a pattern worth watching for quality-control scrutiny at a major dairy/plant-based competitor, though the risk itself is contained to a single discontinued SKU with no illnesses reported.
recommended_action: Monitor for any escalation (illness reports, expanded scope, additional Danone recalls); no action needed now.
date_evidence: FDA recall notice and company PR Newswire release both dated Sept. 15, 2026

title: DOJ Settles Contaminated Infant-Formula Case With Abbott for $385M, Drops Criminal Charges Amid Political-Donation Scrutiny
summary: The Justice Department announced Sept. 14, 2026 that Abbott Laboratories will pay nearly $385 million to settle False Claims Act allegations that it concealed bacterial-contamination findings at its Sturgis, Michigan infant-formula plant, whose 2022 shutdown (tied to Cronobacter sakazakii contamination and several infant illnesses and deaths) triggered a nationwide formula shortage. DOJ leadership closed a parallel criminal investigation in favor of the civil settlement, a more lenient outcome than career prosecutors reportedly believed the evidence supported; the decision has drawn scrutiny after reporting that Abbott donated $500,000 to President Trump's inaugural fund and that Trump later purchased Abbott stock.
why_it_matters: Abbott is an infant-formula maker, not a dairy processor, but this is a live case study in how the current DOJ is exercising discretion on food-safety criminal enforcement -- declining charges despite internal recommendations to prosecute -- and the political-donation narrative now attached to that decision. Any food or infant-nutrition manufacturer facing a serious contamination event should expect this precedent, and the public scrutiny of industry-DOJ ties around it, to shape both enforcement expectations and media framing. A New York state senator has already cited the settlement to press Gov. Hochul to sign the state's pending infant-formula heavy-metal disclosure bill (see watch list).
recommended_action: Brief food-safety/regulatory-affairs leadership on DOJ's enforcement posture in this case and the political scrutiny attached to it; no direct action needed, but monitor for spillover into broader food-safety-enforcement coverage.
date_evidence: DOJ press release URL slug (justice.gov/usao-wdmi/pr/2026_0914_Abbott_Settlement_PR); UPI wire dated Sept. 15, 2026

title: Senate Agriculture Committee Advances Farm Bill 2.0 on 12-11 Party-Line Vote
summary: The Republican-led Senate Agriculture Committee voted 12-11 along party lines on Sept. 16, 2026 to advance the Agricultural Act of 2026 ("Farm Bill 2.0"), reconvening after an Aug. 6 markup failed 10-11 over an unrelated SNAP dispute. Sen. Mitch McConnell, back after a recovery absence, cast a vote; Sens. Ernst and Grassley objected to the bill remaining closed to new amendments but did not block passage. The bill now heads to the full Senate floor, with no vote date yet set.
why_it_matters: The bill's dairy title survives intact: reauthorization of the Dairy Forward Pricing Program, Dairy Indemnity Payment Program and Dairy Promotion and Research Board through 2031, plus a new mandatory dairy-manufacturer cost and yield reporting requirement tied to Federal Milk Marketing Order "make allowance" pricing. Committee passage is a meaningful procedural step after the bill spent six weeks stalled, but a full floor vote and House reconciliation remain before any reporting mandate becomes law.
recommended_action: Brief regulatory-affairs leadership that the dairy cost/yield reporting mandate and program reauthorizations have cleared committee; no filing action needed until floor scheduling or House reconciliation firms up.
date_evidence: article publication date (Agri-Pulse, Sept. 16, 2026)

title: FDA Releases 2026 Food Code
summary: FDA published its 2026 Food Code on Sept. 17, 2026, the model food-safety regulations for retail and food service that state, local, tribal and territorial agencies may adopt. Changes from the 2022 edition include a new written employee-illness-policy requirement, a limited double-gloving exception, an added alternative cooling process for retail foods, and revised food-establishment and mobile-food-establishment definitions.
why_it_matters: The Food Code is the baseline retail/foodservice food-safety standard most states model their own rules on, so any facility-side or foodservice-adjacent operations will eventually see these provisions surface locally; there is nothing dairy-specific in this edition, making it a routine biennial update rather than a new compliance driver.
recommended_action: Monitor Only; no action needed.

title: FDA Executive Summary Reveals Clover Hill Dairy's Fatal Listeria Strain Persisted in Plant Since 2021
summary: FDA published an executive summary of its investigation into the Clover Hill Dairy soft-cheese Listeria outbreak (15 sickened, 1 death, closed in August), revealing that whole-genome sequencing matched the outbreak strain found in the plant's environment to patient samples dating back to 2021 -- five years before the 2026 outbreak was identified. The summary, released alongside one on an unrelated Guatemalan-cantaloupe Salmonella outbreak, is part of a newer FDA practice of publishing post-investigation executive summaries for added transparency.
why_it_matters: The finding shows a resident Listeria strain went undetected in a dairy production environment for roughly five years despite routine sanitation and testing before it caused a fatal outbreak, reinforcing the case for rigorous environmental monitoring programs (including harborage-site and drain testing) at cheese and soft-dairy facilities; FDA may cite this case as it pushes for stronger environmental monitoring expectations industry-wide.
recommended_action: Monitor; useful case reference for QA/food-safety teams on environmental monitoring program rigor for resident Listeria strains; no direct company exposure (isolated regional producer, outbreak already closed).
date_evidence: byline: Food Safety News article dated Sept. 17, 2026, reporting FDA's executive summary release

title: USDA Ends Mandatory Dairy-Checkoff Funding of ESG and Net-Zero Programs
summary: USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins directed the National Dairy Board on Sept. 17 to stop using mandatory dairy-checkoff assessments to fund ESG, net-zero and climate-neutrality initiatives, naming the Innovation Center for U.S. Dairy's Greener Cattle Initiative, U.S. Dairy Net Zero Initiative, Pathways to Dairy Net Zero, Sustainability Alliance and U.S. Dairy Stewardship Commitment, effective immediately; a companion Under Secretary memo extends the same restriction to all USDA commodity checkoff boards. The action follows a June 2026 lawsuit (Swan v. Rollins, E.D. Wis.) by three Wisconsin dairy farmers, represented by the Wisconsin Institute for Law & Liberty, arguing checkoff funds were being used to subsidize climate advocacy farmers did not support; WILL and the American Dairy Coalition publicly welcomed the action same-day.
why_it_matters: The Innovation Center for U.S. Dairy's sustainability infrastructure, including FARM Environmental Stewardship reporting that many processors and retail customers reference in their own environmental claims, has relied on checkoff funding; an immediate cutoff with no transition period creates a program-continuity gap and a reputational crosscurrent, since environmentally-minded retail customers and anti-ESG stakeholders will read this in opposite ways. As of this scan, IDFA, NMPF and the Innovation Center/Dairy Management Inc. had not issued a public response, leaving processors without guidance on what happens to existing reporting commitments and customer-facing claims built on these programs.
recommended_action: Brief leadership now: inventory which checkoff-funded sustainability programs (FARM ES, Net Zero Initiative, Stewardship Commitment) the company participates in or cites in customer/public materials, and prepare a holding statement before customers, employees or press ask; watch for guidance from IDFA, NMPF and DMI/Innovation Center for U.S. Dairy.

sources.outlet: Wisconsin Institute for Law & Liberty (via WisPolitics)

title: CoBank Analysis: Ten States Now Produce 74% of US Milk as Production Consolidates
summary: A Sept. 17, 2026 CoBank analysis by lead dairy economist Corey Geiger finds that 10 states -- California, Wisconsin, Idaho, Texas, New York, Michigan, Minnesota, Pennsylvania, Iowa and New Mexico -- now produce 74% of US milk (84% among the top 14), with growth concentrated in states with available water and new processing investment. Since January 2023, Texas, Idaho, Kansas, South Dakota and Michigan have added dairy cows while Wisconsin's herd has shrunk by about 44,000 head.
why_it_matters: Continued geographic consolidation of US milk supply toward the Great Plains, Southwest and parts of the Upper Midwest has direct implications for a national dairy manufacturer's sourcing, plant-siting, water-risk and logistics planning as new processing capacity follows the milk.
recommended_action: No action needed; share with supply-chain/strategy teams tracking regional milk-supply and processing-investment trends.
date_evidence: Dairy Herd publication dated one day before this Sept. 18 scan, corroborated same-day by eDairy News
